clue.text: Appears as veins in the ear

indicators.note: what reaches the ear is the sound of a word, not its spelling, so we want a soundalike

blocks.note: veins of ore or coal in rock are seams

explanation.surface: Something showing up as veins inside someone's ear, like a medical observation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Veins' tempts you toward blood vessels, but here it means mineral seams in rock.
explanation.definitionFit: To seem is to give an impression or look a certain way, a synonym of appearing.

clue.text: Announce frequently: "Love is on the cutting edge"

blocks.note: to announce something is to state it
oft is an old word for often
the heart stands for love

explanation.surface: A slogan proclaiming that love is the latest fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make Love look like part of a quoted slogan; it is just the last piece, and the definition is the closing phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Something state of the art is the most advanced available, which is what being on the cutting edge describes.

clue.text: Terribly angered!

indicators.note: terribly suggests something done badly or wrecked, so the letters of the next word are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An exclamation that someone is furious.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: rearranging the letters of angered gives a word meaning terribly angered.
explanation.definitionFit: Enraged means furious, which is extreme anger, exactly what terribly angered describes.

clue.text: Discussed light check in underground vehicle?

indicators.note: something discussed is spoken about, so we want words as they sound when said, not as spelt

blocks.note: light means under the required weight, punningly sub-weight
to rein in is to check or restrain

explanation.surface: Talking about checking the lights inside a subway car or mine cart.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, sub-weight rein runs together into the answer; the pun is loose, as sub-weight is not a standard word.
explanation.definitionFit: A subway train runs through tunnels beneath a city, so it is a vehicle travelling below ground; the question mark flags the punning wordplay.

clue.text: Arguing and going out around East Broadway at 1st

indicators.note: the word for going out is wrapped around the following letters, enclosing them
at first means only the opening letter of the street name is used

blocks.note: a couple going out together are dating
E is the compass abbreviation for east
the opening letter of Broadway

explanation.surface: A couple quarrelling as they go out for the evening near East Broadway in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: The East and Broadway pieces sit inside the word for going out, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Debating is arguing a point back and forth, so the two present participles are synonyms.

clue.text: One who breaks the law with reckless speed on winding road

indicators.note: reckless suggests careless, wild movement, so these letters are scrambled
a winding course twists about, so these letters are twisted out of order too

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker tearing along a winding road at reckless speed.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words carry their own scrambling signal, and the two sets of letters are mixed together.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw, a bandit of the Wild West kind who lives outside the law.

clue.text: Infantry?

blocks.note: surface reading: foot soldiers, an army's fighting troops on foot
setter's reading: a group of infants, read as if the word were built from infant

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: soldiers carry arms, and so do mothers carrying babies. It is also the title of a Rodgers and Hart musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Babes in arms are infants too young to walk, carried by adults, a jokey reading of a body of infants.

clue.text: Broadcast in jeans, wearing shirt

indicators.note: a garment that is worn goes around the body, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: a tee is a T-shirt
Levis are a famous brand of jeans

explanation.surface: Appearing on air dressed in jeans and a shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: The jeans go inside the shirt, which is how many people dress.
explanation.definitionFit: To televise is to transmit a programme on television, one kind of broadcasting.

clue.text: Country song, for example: popular but retro

indicators.note: retro means looking back, so the string of pieces is read from the end to the start

blocks.note: an air is a tune or song
e.g. is the abbreviation for for example
something in is fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A country-and-western number described as popular yet old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country song' reads as one phrase meaning a country-music number; the definition is Country alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigeria is a nation in West Africa, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: They need oxygen when dress is engulfed by receding water

indicators.note: receding means going back, so the word for water is read backwards
being engulfed means being swallowed up inside something else

blocks.note: the sea is a body of water
a robe is a long dress or gown

explanation.surface: Someone's dress being swallowed by a retreating tide, needing air.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed water word is split after its first letter to take in the dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerobes are organisms that require oxygen to live, the opposite of anaerobic microbes.

clue.text: CO2, for instance, trails migrant blue whales

indicators.note: a migrant moves from place to place, so these letters move out of their order

blocks.note: the four letters of blue, rearranged
carbon dioxide is an example of a gas

explanation.surface: Carbon dioxide exhaled behind migrating blue whales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trails' means comes after, so the gas goes at the end; 'migrant blue whales' wants to be a species, but whales alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Belugas are small white Arctic whales, so the plural names a group of whales.

clue.text: What paparazzi might be doing with meteors

blocks.note: first meaning: photographers taking pictures of celebrities
second meaning: streaks of light across the night sky

explanation.surface: Photographers snapping away at a meteor shower.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads the phrase as a verb (photographing celebrities), the second as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrities are stars and photographers shoot them; meteors are popularly called falling stars in the night sky.

clue.text: Free verse rang for printers

indicators.note: free verse has no fixed form, and freed letters are released into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Free verse ringing out for the people who print it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free verse' reads as a poetry term, but Free is the signal for the letters that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Engravers cut images into plates from which pictures are printed, so they are a kind of printmaker.

clue.text: A sign of renewed vigor

indicators.note: something renewed is remade, so these letters are made over in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An indication that someone has their energy back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A sign of renewed vigor' reads as a symptom of health; the sign is one of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgo, the Virgin, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac in astrology.

clue.text: Overdose, if making a comeback, is a 20?

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the pieces are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: OD is the standard abbreviation for overdose
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether an overdose that returns counts as clue 20.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to 20 Down, PET NAME; the question mark marks this answer as one example of that.
explanation.definitionFit: Fido is the classic name given to a pet dog, an example of a pet name.

clue.text: F—after this you'd want to try again

definitions.text: F—after this you'd want to try again

blocks.note: surface reading: a failing grade, after which you would want to retake the test

blocks.clueFragment: after this you'd want to try again
blocks.note: setter's reading: F followed by a dash is a word broken off after one letter, a botched beginning, as when a runner jumps the gun and the race must restart

explanation.walkthrough: F with a dash looks like a failing mark or a bleeped swear word, but it is simply a word begun and abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A false start is a beginning that has to be scrapped, as in a race where runners go before the gun and must line up again.

clue.text: Maritime magnate — bam! — sports a black eye

indicators.note: to sport something is to wear it, so one word is worn around the other

blocks.note: a shiner is slang for a black eye
pow is a comic-book punch noise like bam

explanation.surface: A shipping tycoon punched and left with a black eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The punch sound goes inside the black-eye word after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipowner owns merchant vessels, and a rich one is a tycoon of the seas.

clue.text: Monk and fur trader?

blocks.note: first meaning: a member of a strict Catholic order known for vows of silence
second meaning, playful: someone who sets traps, as a fur trapper does, with a job suffix like florist

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the second meaning is invented: the word is read as trap plus a job ending.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trappist is a Cistercian monk of La Trappe; a fur trapper catches animals in traps, which the joke reading suggests.

clue.text: Man's small combo, largely pleasant and theatrical

indicators.note: largely means for the most part but not wholly, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: belonging to a man is his
a small band of three players
nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A man's little jazz group, mostly agreeable and rather showy.
explanation.walkthrough: A combo is a small jazz band, and the smallest common one has three players.
explanation.definitionFit: Histrionic means exaggerated and stagey in manner, a synonym of theatrical behaviour.

clue.text: Inside, Brahms met an Austrian composer

indicators.note: inside says the letters lie within the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the last letter of Brahms, all of met and an, and the first letter of Austrian

explanation.surface: Brahms meeting a composer from Austria.
explanation.walkthrough: The Austrian composer looks like the definition, but this composer was Czech; Austrian only supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedrich Smetana was a Czech nineteenth-century composer, best known for Ma Vlast and The Bartered Bride.

clue.text: Frank O'Hara's chief writing implement

indicators.note: the chief part of a word is its head, the letter at the front

blocks.note: the head letter of the poet's surname
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: The favourite pen of the American poet Frank O'Hara.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like the poet's first name, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being open means honest and candid, the adjective sense of frank.

clue.text: Rose, while holding up man and baby, say

indicators.note: holding something means having it within your grasp, so one word goes inside the other
in a down clue, up means the word is written bottom to top, so read backwards

blocks.note: Pete Rose was a famous American baseball player
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman named Rose lifting a man and a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: Rose looks like a woman's name or a flower; it is the surname of Pete Rose, the baseball star.
explanation.definitionFit: Baby is a term of endearment, an affectionate name used for someone close to you.

clue.text: See 5
Loved at the cusp, oddly

indicators.note: oddly means taking the letters in odd-numbered positions only

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters of these words

explanation.surface: Someone loved on the brink of something, in a strange way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the cusp' sounds like a turning point, but its letters are the source.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat something up is an idiom for relishing it eagerly, as in a crowd adoring a performer.

clue.text: What the diligent student did — or the bank robber?

blocks.note: first meaning: wrote down points from a lecture
second meaning: stole banknotes

explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads notes as jottings, the second as paper money.
explanation.definitionFit: A careful student records written jottings in class, while a thief makes off with paper currency, both called notes.

clue.text: See 3
Empress's wrap grabbed by returning soldier, perhaps

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the soldier word is read backwards
something grabbed is held tight inside another's grip

blocks.note: a soldier ant is one kind of ant
a sari is a wrapped Indian garment

explanation.surface: A soldier on his way home seizing an empress's shawl.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for is, joining the definition to the wordplay; soldier, perhaps signals an insect, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the wife of a tsar or a Russian ruler in her own right, an empress.

clue.text: Grandma hugs Irving — what bliss!

indicators.note: hugging someone wraps your arms around them, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: nana is a familiar name for a grandmother
Irv is the short form of the name Irving

explanation.surface: A grandmother embracing her grandson Irving in pure joy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as an exclamation; it means the state of bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana is a state of perfect happiness, from the Buddhist ideal of release from suffering.

clue.text: Fears net is broken with a snap

indicators.note: something broken falls apart, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Worries that a net will tear with a sudden crack.
explanation.walkthrough: Snap sounds like the noise of breaking, but it is a press stud on clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap is a press stud that clips two pieces of fabric together, one kind of clothes closure.

clue.text: Shortz and vanden Heuvel pursuing silence in huts

blocks.note: sh is the call for silence
Will Shortz edits the New York Times crossword and Katrina vanden Heuvel edited The Nation, so they are editors

explanation.surface: Two well-known American editors chasing quiet in rustic cabins.
explanation.walkthrough: Pursuing means following, so the editors come after the silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheds are small simple outbuildings, much the same as huts.
